payload.rationale: I estimate a 35% chance that Cleveland wins. The supplied evidence places Cleveland on the road in Tampa Bay after a 34–10 opening loss, while Tampa Bay lost 33–27. Those results favor Tampa Bay directionally, but one game without opponent adjustment is weak evidence of underlying strength. Cleveland also has guard Teven Jenkins ruled out and cornerback Tyson Campbell questionable; Tampa Bay has three questionable players. I give the availability report modest weight because questionable does not mean unavailable. The estimate combines a general home-field advantage assumption with a heavily discounted reading of the opening results, rather than treating the scoring margins as a stable performance gap. The strongest reason this estimate could be too high is that Cleveland’s low scoring reflects a persistent offensive weakness, compounded by the missing guard. The strongest reason it could be too low is that the opening margins primarily reflect opponent quality or game-specific noise; Tampa Bay’s 33 points conceded and possible secondary absences could leave Cleveland a favorable matchup. This is a probability of an outright Cleveland win, not a payout estimate that awards half credit for a tie.
limitations: Only one 2026 regular-season result per team is supplied, with no opponent-strength adjustment.
No complete current roster, quarterback assessment, final inactive list, weather report, or fitted matchup model is available.
Questionable injury designations do not establish whether players will play or how limited they will be.
Ties are not Cleveland wins; fractional settlements and cancelled or invalid events are excluded from eventual binary scoring.
